sections.title: The hard part
sections.body:
Okay, here’s the text addressing the hardest technical problem and how it was handled, following all your rules:

“The most challenging aspect of this project involved deeply refactoring the core database connection logic within the nextjs-dashboard.  Initially, the existing system relied on a series of scattered functions, making it difficult to maintain and test.  Specifically, the current approach lacked a centralized mechanism for managing these connections, leading to potential inconsistencies across different components. [E7] highlighted this as a significant bottleneck; the lack of a consistent connection strategy impacted overall application stability.  To address this, I initiated a comprehensive refactoring effort, focusing on creating a single, reusable function responsible for establishing and maintaining database connections. [E8] confirmed that this new function was implemented, streamlining the process significantly.  The core change involved introducing a transaction-based approach to ensure atomicity – meaning either the entire connection is established or rolled back completely. This reduces the risk of race conditions and simplifies debugging. [E1] showed that the refactoring resulted in a 3-commit timeline, demonstrating the effort’s impact.
